system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Global Order: Debt, Wars, Energy and Tech Rivalries
system_description.narrative_summary: A brittle, interconnected global system is being pulled by three dominant stresses: acute fiscal and bond-market strain in the United States that is eroding policy credibility and the dollar’s safe‑haven status; simultaneous regional wars and geopolitical flashpoints (Iran‑Hormuz, Russia‑Ukraine, Israel‑Gaza, North Korea/Taiwan) driving energy, food and defence shocks; and strategic economic competition and domestic financial stress in major powers (China’s property collapse, US‑China tech/trade frictions, rising tariff conflicts). These dynamics amplify each other through markets, supply chains and alliances, producing cascading risks for trade, energy flows and financial stability.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and their fiscal/monetary policies; sovereign debt and global bond markets; multinational corporations and supply chains (energy, chips, shipping); military forces and alliance structures; trade agreements, sanctions and trade barriers; strategic infrastructure and logistics (straits, canals, refineries).
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-political-economic system (the integrated global economy, security order and ecological/commodity systems).
adjacent_subsystems: Global Financial System (sovereign debt, central banks, capital markets)
Global Energy & Commodities System (oil, gas, food, shipping chokepoints)
Regional Security Complexes (Middle East, Europe‑Russia, East Asia)

variables.name: Global bond market stress & US fiscal strain
variables.description: The United States, global investors and central banks are negotiating a new balance between fiscal expansion and monetary policy as soaring US debt and Treasury interventions (buybacks) destabilize bond markets, the dollar and safe‑asset hierarchies.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and Western support dynamics
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed variably by NATO and Western suppliers, remain locked in an intensifying military struggle marked by strategic strikes, mobilization and pressures on allied weapon stocks and aid commitments.

variables.name: US–Iran confrontation and Gulf energy chokepoint
variables.description: The United States, Iran and Gulf actors (with secondary involvement from China and regional states) are engaged in escalating economic and military confrontation that is shifting commercial flows and threatening the Strait of Hormuz and global energy supplies.

variables.name: US–China strategic tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting technological leadership, supply chains and trade rules—via tariffs, export controls, investment scrutiny and third‑party pressure—which is reshaping global semiconductor, rare‑earths and high‑tech markets.

variables.name: North Korea missile–nuclear escalation
variables.description: North Korea and the US‑South Korea‑Japan security constellation are experiencing a renewed cycle of missile launches, nuclear capability reassessments and fraught diplomacy that raises acute regional flashpoint risks.
